name: pseudo-localization
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: Pseudo-localise strings in Node to test text expansion, accents and RTL before translations exist
summary: pseudo-localization (npm) turns a string into accented, lengthened look-alike text (pseudoLocalizeString, strategies accented and bidi) so a title, lower third or caption can be checked for overflow and missing glyphs before real translations exist. A pure string function; its DOM observer is not needed for media.
use_when: Stress-testing title boxes and kinetic type for localisation growth before translation
Finding glyphs a scene font cannot draw, using accented look-alike text
A version-set check for the adaptation skill, where real translations do not exist yet
avoid_when: Real translations or voice-over fit: translators and the adaptation skill
True right-to-left shaping checks: render real RTL copy in a browser
Typography review of finished text: typographer agent
notes: 2026-11-27: lead data matched npm (3.1.3, MIT). The accented strategy doubles vowels (about 25% longer) and the bidi strategy wraps text in RLO and PDF controls with upside-down look-alikes, not mirrored layout.

assessment.rationale: MIT, one dependency-free string function, npm 3.1.3 published 2026-09-24. Nothing else in the catalogue generates localisation stress text; useful as a cheap text-expansion fixture for version sets, narrow in scope.

evidence.result: Three titles accented: 7 to 9, 20 to 25, 28 to 35 characters; ink 164 to 212, 476 to 596, 667 to 835 px; longest overflowed a 760 px box; identical across two Node 22.19.0 processes; 19 code points absent from JetBrains Mono Bold reported by resvg 0.47.0 and seen as tofu.
evidence.scope: pseudoLocalizeString accented and bidi on three English titles, one monospace font, resvg on macOS arm64; not DOM mode, browser RLO layout, wrapping or real translations.
